They may choose to elect their own combat pay, their spouse's combat pay separately, or both of their combat pay should they each have combat pay.

Fact.Name: Earned income credit (EITC)
Fact.Description:
Earned income credit (EITC) (line 27 1040)
We calculate the EITC up to four times -- EITC may be calculated with: 1. No combat pay (for people without combat pay, and people who elect not to include their combat pay) 2. With the primary filer's combat pay 3. With the secondary filer's combat pay 4. With both filer's combined combat pay.
If a user qualifies for more than 1 of those options (most taxpayers do not have combat pay and will therefore default into the "no combat pay" option), we guide the taxpayer towards electing the combat pay option that will give them the most EITC.

Fact.Name: The amount of the Earned Income Tax Credit without combat pay
Fact.Description: The section 32(a) earned income credit computed on this return's earned income with NO section 32(c)(2)(B)(vi) combat pay election. It is the credit percentage of earned income up to the earned income amount, reduced by the phaseout percentage of the excess of adjusted gross income (or earned income, if greater) over the phaseout amount, floored at $0 and held to the AGI-side limit /maxEitcFromAGI that section 32(a)(2)(B) imposes. The earned income leg it reads is /eitcRoundedEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay. Every year-indexed figure it consumes — /eitcMaxCredit, /eitcPhaseInRate, /eitcPhaseOutRate, /eitcPhaseOutThreshold, /eitcPhaseoutAmountLowerBound and /eitcCompletedPhaseoutAmount — is carried on this module's own parameter facts and is governed for TY2025 by Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §.06 Earned Income Credit; no indexed amount is written here. The $24 and $25 literals in the body are section 32(f)(2) table mechanics, not indexed figures: the credit is read off a table whose income brackets are $50 wide, so a bracket's top is the rounded midpoint plus $24 and the phaseout is measured from the bracket midpoint, the threshold plus $25.

Fact.Name: Compensation received for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution
Fact.Description:
The amount the taxpayer received for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution. §32(c)(2)(B)(iv) excludes it from "earned income" for the EIC; it is NOT excluded from AGI or gross income, and its printed home is Schedule 1 line 8u. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means $0, the pre-existing behavior for every return that doesn't attest this income.
THE GENERAL QUESTION, AND THE ROUTER CARRIES THE SCOPING. This is the ONLY place the dictionary collects this dollar figure, and both consumers read it: the Schedule 1 line 8u placement income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages and the EIC exclusion /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome. Which one gets it is decided by income:/writableIncarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome, so this question must be asked in general terms — a filer who correctly kept the amount off line 1a still has to enter it here, or it reaches no line at all.
THE NAME IS GENERAL ON PURPOSE, not tied to either consumer's placement: the placement itself is decided downstream by income:/writableIncarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome, so a Name naming one placement would misdescribe the return that takes the other branch. See /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation for the printed chain and /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome for the gate.

Fact.Name: Inmate penal-institution compensation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Round(/writableInmatePenalInstitutionCompensation when answered, else 0) — the IsComplete pattern (as /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss) inside the the rounding adjudication rounding boundary. Firewalls /eitcEarnedIncomeBase from the writable's own completeness: a bare Dependency on an unanswered writable propagates that writable's completeness upward through Add/Subtract/GreaterOf, which would turn /eitcEarnedIncomeBase (and everything downstream of it) from Complete to Placeholder for every return that doesn't attest this income — a real regression, not merely a value change. This Switch's catch-all branch supplies a literal $0, which is unconditionally Complete, so /eitcEarnedIncomeBase stays Complete exactly as before, and Round of a Complete value is Complete.
The rounding adjudication: the Round is the printed-line boundary, not a convenience. This exclusion HAS a printed line of its own, Schedule 1 line 8u ("Wages earned while incarcerated. Enter the amount that you received for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution"), and a schedule line sits squarely inside the page 23 election's own scope ("You can round off cents to whole dollars on your return and schedules ... you must round all amounts"), which this dictionary took globally. So the attested figure is whole where it is printed and the cents stop there, before the Pub. 596 $50-row StepwiseMultiply in /eitcRoundedEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay and its three combat-pay siblings ever see them. Before the rounding adjudication this leg was a raw Dollar writable subtracted with cents intact, and the combat-pay rounding settlement's premise that combat pay would be the first cents to reach that lookup was false because of it. Same settlement as the combat-pay rounding settlement, one layer down: the cents stop at the printed line.
WHAT THIS FACT IS, AFTER THE LINE 8u BUILD. It is the ATTESTED AMOUNT — whole, complete-safe, and neutral as to where the dollars landed. It is no longer itself the subtrahend: the EIC exclusion is /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome, which reads this fact through the income-side router, and the Schedule 1 line 8u placement income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages reads it through the other arm of that same router. The two consumers partition this value; their sum is always exactly this value. The Round below stays HERE, at the one place both consumers inherit it from, so the the rounding adjudication settlement is unchanged in substance and in every committed number.
The placement adjudication: THE SUBTRACTION WAS UNCONDITIONAL, AND THE LINE 8u BUILD MADE IT CONDITIONAL, by the route the placement adjudication itself specified. The placement adjudication asked whether this leg should be gated on where the amount was reported, since the printed instruction keeps inmate wages OUT of line 1z. The placement adjudication held the premise CORRECT and the conclusion premature: gating alone would have made the EITC right on a return whose TOTAL INCOME was then wrong by the same amount, because no 8u surface existed for the amount to land on. the line 8u build built that surface and applied the gate in the one commit the coupling clause demanded, so the objection is discharged rather than overruled. The paragraphs below are preserved as the derivation that got there; where they say a routing surface does not exist, read "did not exist before the line 8u build". The workfare half is unaffected and its own reasons stay on /subsidizedWorkfareCompensation.
THE PRINTED CHAIN, RE-DERIVED. The EIC Step 5 earned-income worksheet prints exactly one subtraction, and its subtrahend is the one amount whose own Schedule 1 line says the amount is INSIDE line 1z: line 8s, "Nontaxable amount of Medicaid waiver payments INCLUDED ON FORM 1040, LINE 1a OR 1d" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, pages 23, 92, PDF pages 92 and 23). Line 8u is the opposite shape — "Wages earned while incarcerated. ENTER THE AMOUNT THAT YOU RECEIVED for services performed while an inmate in a penal institution" (6675-6685) — a PLACEMENT line, not a back-out line, which is exactly why the line-1a CAUTION can say "Do not report these wages on line 1a" (1378-1388). The worksheet needs no inmate subtraction because line 8u has already routed the amount out of 1z. That contrast between 8s and 8u is the whole discriminator, and it answers the placement adjudication's framing question directly: 8u is NOT an "amount included on 1a in error" reporting line; 8s is the line of that kind, and it is the one the worksheet subtracts.
THAT ABSENCE IS A READING OF THE WHOLE BLOCK, NOT A QUOTATION, and is recorded as such rather than dressed as a cite. The verifiable claim is the ENUMERATION of the Step 5 worksheet at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 42 (PDF page 42): line 1 "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 1z"; line 2 the Schedule 1 line 8s Medicaid waiver amount; line 3 "Subtract line 2 from line 1"; line 4 elected nontaxable combat pay; line 5 "Add lines 3 and 4. This is your earned income". Five lines, no inmate line, no workfare line. A reader checks the enumeration, not a span.
BUT THE PRINTED CHAIN REACHED THAT RESULT WITH A ROUTING SURFACE THIS DICTIONARY DID NOT HAVE, and that is what decides the issue. There was no Schedule 1 line 8u fact anywhere in dictionary/ty2025 (a grep for "8u" and "incarcerat" across the shipping modules returned this file and nothing else); income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome carried legs for lines 8b, 8d, 8f, 8g, 8h and 8i and no 8u; and line 1h, income:/otherEarnedIncome, is fed solely by pre-minimum-retirement-age disability pensions, with no free-form writable behind it. line 1h is no longer fed SOLELY by disability pensions - it now also carries the IRC 402(g) excess-elective-deferral inclusion, per filer. That does not disturb this fact's reasoning: the new leg is still DERIVED with no free-form writable behind it, so inmate compensation remains unrepresentable on line 1h and the unconditional subtraction below is unchanged. Every route by which inmate compensation could enter this graph — a Form W-2 box 1 through formW2s to line 1a, or a Form 1099 through Schedule C to the Schedule SE line-3 chain — landed it INSIDE the minuend this fact was subtracted from. So the compliant filer's return was NOT REPRESENTABLE here, the population the placement adjudication names as harmed could not be built, and the unconditional subtraction was correct for every return that could be.
AND A BARE ATTESTATION GATE WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE GAP, which is the load-bearing half and the reason the line 8u build had to be a two-halves-in-one-commit unit rather than a gate. The placement adjudication's design 2 ON ITS OWN would make the EITC right on a return whose TOTAL INCOME is wrong by the same amount: with no 8u leg the attested figure reaches no income line at all. A half-fix that corrects one number, leaves the other wrong, and LOOKS adjudicated is the worse outcome, and it is the outcome design 2 alone buys. the line 8u build pairs the gate with the placement, so neither number is left wrong, and that is pinned rather than argued per the the combat-pay rounding settlement standard: tests/nodes/ty2025/income/l8u-incarcerated-wages-routed-to-line-8u asserts /totalIncome 26000 and /eitcEarnedIncomeBase 20000 on an attested 6,000, and its unrouted twin l8u-incarcerated-wages-included-in-reported-wages asserts 20000 and 14000 on the same figure.
THE 8u SURFACE IS BUILT (the line 8u build). income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages now SHIPS; its coupling clause named this fact and obliged the filling unit to re-decide the subtraction in the same commit, and the line 8u build did, by the second of the two options that clause offered. The two assert rows above stay GREEN and unchanged in tests/nodes/ty2025/eitc/inmate-wages-excluded-from-earned-income, because that case leaves income:/writableIncarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome unanswered — the preserving arm — so it is still the population whose inmate wages are inside line 1z. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (FTB 3514 CA earned income exclusion).

Fact.Name: Inmate penal-institution compensation that is INSIDE the reported earned income — the §32(c)(2)(B)(iv) subtrahend
Fact.Description:
The §32(c)(2)(B)(iv) exclusion actually subtracted at /eitcEarnedIncomeBase: /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation when the attested amount is inside the wages or self-employment income this return reports, and $0 when it is not. The discriminator is income:/incarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome, the complete-safe router the line 8u build added ; its FALSE/unanswered arm is the pre-existing behaviour, so this fact equals /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation on every return authored before the line 8u build and on every return that never answers the router.
THIS IS THE OTHER HALF OF A PARTITION, NOT AN EXTRA GATE. The same attested dollars go to exactly one of two places, decided by one boolean:
income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages + /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome == /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation
Subtracting here is right precisely when the amount is inside the minuend (income:/employerIncomeSubtotal + scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome), and $0 is right precisely when the amount went to Schedule 1 line 8u instead, because line 8u feeds Form 1040 line 8 and line 8 is not in that minuend. Neither arm double-counts and neither double-excludes; that is what the placement adjudication asked for and what the contract's coupling clause obliged the 8u build to deliver in the same commit.
WHY THE GATE IS HERE AND NOT AT /eitcEarnedIncomeBase. That fact carries the the rounding adjudication seam finding that it must hold NO Round and no re-shaping of its own — all four operands arrive already whole. Putting the routing Switch here keeps the seam a plain Subtract, keeps the whole-minus-whole argument intact, and leaves the workfare leg untouched: §32(c)(2)(B)(v) reaches only an amount "described in subparagraph (A)", i.e. one that IS includible in gross income, so the workfare subtrahend has no analogous routing question and /subsidizedWorkfareCompensation is still subtracted directly.
direction: the $0 arm fires ONLY when the filer has affirmatively said the amount is outside the reported wage/self-employment income, in which case $0 is the CORRECT subtrahend rather than a gap leg — subtracting anything there would UNDER-state earned income and under-state or deny the EIC, the taxpayer-unfavourable double-exclusion the placement adjudication named. If the router is answered wrongly TRUE by a filer whose wages ARE inside line 1z, earned income is OVER-stated (taxpayer-favourable on the credit) while total income is over-stated too; that residual is recorded in full on income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages.

Fact.Name: Subsidized workfare compensation (TANF work activities) — the TAXABLE part, included in the wages or self-employment income already reported on this return
Fact.Description:
The amount, already included above in wages or self-employment earned income, that the taxpayer received for services performed in work activities described in section 407(d)(4) or (7) of the Social Security Act, to which the taxpayer was assigned under a State TANF program under part A of title IV of that Act, to the extent the payment was subsidized under that State program. §32(c)(2)(B)(v) excludes it from "earned income" for the EIC. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means $0 (no exclusion), the pre-existing behavior.
The placement adjudication sub-point 2, THE FACE CORRECTION, and here the statute writes the scoping itself. §32(c)(2)(B)(v) excludes "no amount DESCRIBED IN SUBPARAGRAPH (A)", and subparagraph (A) is "(i) wages, salaries, tips, and other employee compensation, BUT ONLY IF SUCH AMOUNTS ARE INCLUDIBLE IN GROSS INCOME for the taxable year, plus (ii) the amount of the taxpayer's net earnings from self-employment" (26 U.S.C. 32, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section32&num=0&edition=2024). So the statutory operand is either an amount includible in gross income — hence on a wage line, hence inside Form 1040 line 1z — or net self-employment earnings. It is in-base by construction, which is why the word TAXABLE now leads the Name: a NONTAXABLE workfare payment is not what this fact asks for, is not "described in subparagraph (A)", and is never in line 1z to be subtracted from. See /subsidizedWorkfareCompensation for the Pub. 596 reconciliation that disposes of the placement adjudication's second sub-point.

Fact.Name: Subsidized workfare compensation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
Round(/writableSubsidizedWorkfareCompensation when answered, else 0) — the IsComplete pattern (as /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss) inside the the rounding adjudication rounding boundary. Firewalls /eitcEarnedIncomeBase from the writable's own completeness — see /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation's description for why a bare Dependency on the raw writable would be wrong here.
The rounding adjudication: the Round is the WEAKER of the two legs and is labelled as such. Unlike the inmate exclusion, this one has NO printed line of its own anywhere in Pub. 596 or the Form 1040 instructions — the printed text gives the exclusion (Pub. 596 "Workfare payments") and no placement at all. It rounds at the leg because that is the only shape the printed chain models: every printed subtraction into EIC Step 5 earned income draws its subtrahend from a printed line, including the one subtraction the Step 5 worksheet itself prints (line 2, the Medicaid waiver amounts "excluded from income on Schedule 1, line 8s"), which is also the printed chain's own model for subtracting a NONTAXABLE amount from earned income. Read the full adjudication, the rejected alternatives and the direction note on /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation.
The placement adjudication sub-point 2: REFUTED OUTRIGHT, and on cleaner ground than its sibling leg. The rounding adjudication left the tension that §32(c)(2)(B)(v)'s "described in subparagraph (A)" wording requires an amount includible in gross income while Pub. 596's gloss calls these payments nontaxable, so that a truly nontaxable amount is never inside line 1z and subtracting it would double exclude. The two texts are not competing readings of one amount. They govern DISJOINT POPULATIONS, and the statute writes the inclusion test into the operand itself.
THE STATUTE. §32(c)(2)(B)(v) excludes "no amount described in subparagraph (A)" received for the section 407(d)(4)/(7) work activities, and subparagraph (A) is "(i) wages, salaries, tips, and other employee compensation, but only if such amounts are includible in gross income for the taxable year, plus (ii) the amount of the taxpayer's net earnings from self-employment for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 32, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section32&num=0&edition=2024). Every amount the exclusion can reach is therefore either includible in gross income — hence on a wage line, hence inside Form 1040 line 1z — or net self-employment earnings, hence inside the Schedule SE line-3 chain. IN-BASE BY CONSTRUCTION. There is no gate to write, because Congress already wrote it: an amount outside the base is not "described in subparagraph (A)" and this exclusion never reaches it.
THE PUB. 596 GLOSS. "Workfare payments. NONTAXABLE workfare payments aren't earned income for the EIC" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p596.pdf, page 9, PDF page 9) is a subhead inside the section headed "Income That Is Not Earned Income" (538-540), whose operative instruction is "Don't INCLUDE any of these items in your earned income" (477-479 — the two-column extraction splits the sentence, "Don't in-" on 477 and the rest on 479). That is an inclusion rule, never a subtraction rule, over the population that is nontaxable and therefore never in line 1z at all — the same rule the pub states generally at 451-455, "Employee pay is earned income only if it is taxable. Nontaxable employee pay ... isn't earned income." Nothing to subtract for that population; nothing conditional about the taxable subsidized one this fact asks for. Two mechanisms, two populations, no contradiction, and the writable's Name now leads with TAXABLE so an intake surface cannot collect the wrong one.
SO THE LEG IS UNCHANGED and the rounding adjudication's second tension is discharged rather than re-parked. THIS one is subtracted DIRECTLY and unconditionally at /eitcEarnedIncomeBase, with no routing wrapper, because the STATUTE'S OWN WORDS put the inclusion test inside the operand.
THE TWO LEGS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, and each verdict is recorded on its own fact rather than once for both. Absent a routing surface, both would land the same way for different reasons: this one on the statute, the inmate one on a REPRESENTABILITY finding about this dictionary — there was no Schedule 1 line 8u surface for an inmate amount to sit outside line 1z on. Now that surface exists, so the inmate leg is GATED behind a router (/inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome, reading income:/incarceratedWagesOutsideReportedIncome) and this one is not. The asymmetry is the point: a workfare amount that IS "described in subparagraph (A)" is includible in gross income by definition, so it has no line-8u-shaped escape route and needs no router. If a future unit ever finds one, it belongs here and not on the sibling.

Fact.Name: EITC earned income base (wages plus self-employment)
Fact.Description:
Earned income for the EITC: W-2-type earned income (employerIncomeSubtotal) plus net self-employment earned income (Schedule C net profit minus the deductible half of SE tax), minus the §32(c)(2)(B)(iv)/(v) inmate-compensation and subsidized-workfare exclusions (read through their complete-safe wrappers, /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome — since the line 8u build, the ROUTED wrapper — and /subsidizedWorkfareCompensation), floored at 0. Combat-pay variants add nontaxable combat pay on top of this. Not a wages-only base; the exclusion subtraction is additive — both complete-safe wrappers default to $0, so every return that doesn't attest this income computes byte-identical to before, AND stays Complete (not merely $0) exactly as before, because the wrappers firewall the raw writables' completeness rather than exposing it here.
THE SEAM IS WHOLE BY CONSTRUCTION, AND CARRIES NO ROUND OF ITS OWN. All four operands are already whole where their own printed lines are: income:/employerIncomeSubtotal Rounds at Form 1040 line 1z, scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome Rounds at the Schedule SE line 3 chain, and since the rounding adjudication both exclusion wrappers Round at their own printed images. A whole minuend less whole subtrahends is whole, and GreaterOf(whole, 0) is whole, so every one of this fact's five readers gets a whole-dollar figure: the Pub. 596 $50-row StepwiseMultiply in /eitcRoundedEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay, the three combat-pay arms /earnedIncomePlus{Primary,Spouse,BothTP}CombatPay (each adding an already-whole line-1i figure per the combat-pay rounding settlement), and the /belowEitcEarnedIncomeLimit comparison. Adding a Round here as well would not be belt-and-braces: it would ship the rounding adjudication's REJECTED design 2, whose value differs from this one whenever the two exclusions' cents cross a half dollar in aggregate. The reading, its two honest limits and the rejected alternatives live on /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensation.
THE TWO SUBTRAHENDS ARE NOT ALIKE (the placement adjudication, closed by the line 8u build), and both of the rounding adjudication's honest limits are discharged rather than carried. The WORKFARE leg needs no inclusion gate and still has none: its operand is in-base by the statute's own words (§32(c)(2)(B)(v) reaches only an amount "described in subparagraph (A)", which is includible-in-gross-income employee compensation or net self-employment earnings). The INMATE leg USED to need none for a weaker reason — this dictionary had no Schedule 1 line 8u routing for the amount to sit outside of, so every intake that could carry inmate compensation fed one of this Subtract's two minuend terms. the line 8u build built that routing (income:/schedule1Line8uIncarceratedWages) and so had to build the gate with it, which is exactly what the contract's coupling clause obliged: this Subtract now takes /inmatePenalInstitutionCompensationInEarnedIncome, which is the attested amount when it is inside this minuend and $0 when it went to Form 1040 line 8 instead. The verdicts and their spans stay on the wrapper facts, one each, because the two legs are now settled for genuinely different reasons.
THIS SEAM'S OWN SHAPE IS UNCHANGED — still a bare Subtract of whole subtrahends from a whole minuend, still no Round. The routing Switch lives one level down, on the wrapper, precisely so the the rounding adjudication argument above survives the change.
EIC WORKSHEET B PART 3 — A THIRD MINUEND TERM, and it is the companion half of a change made in another module, not an addition on its own account. Statutory employee box 1 wages now leave Form 1040 line 1a (formW2s:/wages) and line 1z (income:/{primary,secondary}FilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase) because the printed instruction enters them on Schedule C line 1 instead. Worksheet B is the EIC's own answer to that: Part 2 says "Don't include on these lines any statutory employee income", and Part 3 line 3 then says "Enter the amount from Schedule C, line 1, that you are filing as a statutory employee", which line 4b combines with lines 1e, 2c and 4a into total earned income. So the amount is an ADDEND on top of the Step 5 figure, and without this term a statutory employee's box 1 would reach this base through no term at all once the line 1z subtraction is in — a credit denied on income IRC 32(c)(2)(A)(i) counts as earned. That false denial is the defect this leg exists to prevent, and it is pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/eitc/statutory-employee-wages-stay-in-eic-earned-income.
THE PART 2 HALF LANDED the same day (scheduleSE reads the gated per-filer Schedule C totals), so this base computes Worksheet B end to end on a statutory return.

Fact.Name: EITC investment income
Fact.Description: Publication 596 Worksheet 1 line 14, the earned income credit's investment income: the total of worksheet lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 10 and 13 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p596.pdf, page 7). /belowEitcInvestmentIncomeLimit compares it with the line 15 limit. LINE 1 is taxable interest (Form 1040 line 2b). LINE 2 is one printed line with two sources, "Enter any amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a, plus any amount on Form 8814, line 1b" (line 362): interest:/taxExemptInterest plus form8814:/form8814TotalTaxExemptInterest, nested in one sub-Add so the printed line stays one line. The Form 8814 addend is the WHOLE of line 1b; the worksheet applies no private-activity-bond portioning, which belongs to Form 6251 line 2g and reads a different form8814 fact (/form8814PrivateActivityBondInterest). Reading the portion here would under-state investment income and over-allow the credit. LINE 3 is ordinary dividends (Form 1040 line 3b). LINE 4 reads "Enter the amount from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8z, that is from Form 8814 if you are filing that form to report your child's interest and dividend income on your return" (lines 364-367). That amount is form8814:/form8814Pub596Worksheet2Line10Total: the child's ordinary inclusion over the $2,700 base amount (form8814:/form8814TotalLine12OtherIncome, the figure income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome carries into line 8z), summed over the attached Forms 8814, less the Alaska Permanent Fund part Worksheet 2 takes out when a child received an Alaska Permanent Fund dividend (the worksheet's parenthetical, "If your child received an Alaska Permanent Fund dividend, use Worksheet 2 in this chapter to figure the amount to enter on this line"). With no Alaska Permanent Fund amount answered it equals line 12. A nonzero line 12 raises investment income and can deny the credit on its own merits. The child's line 9 qualified dividends reach this worksheet through line 3 (income:/ordinaryDividends, Form 1040 line 3b) and line 10 through line 5 (income:/capitalGainsOrLosses, line 7a), so neither is wired again and nothing is counted twice. LINE 7 is Form 1040 line 7a (a loss enters as zero) less the Form 4797 gain on line 6 (form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion), floored at zero (lines 369-375). LINE 10 is royalty income and personal-property rental income less their expenses, floored once (lines 377-385): scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome (Schedule E line 23b royalties already net of their line 20 expenses) plus income:/schedule1Line8lIncomeOrZero less income:/schedule1Line24bRentalOfPersonalPropertyExpensesOrZero. LINE 13 combines the passive-activity income of line 11 and the passive-activity losses of line 12, floored once (lines 386-394): scheduleE:/overallPassiveNet (the Schedule E passive activities, including line 40) plus /form4797Line10PassiveOrdinaryGain (a Form 4797 line 10 passive ordinary gain or loss). Example (line 12 $10,799, Alaska Permanent Fund part $800, line 4 $9,999; with $1,200 of parent interest the total is $11,199 and the credit is allowed, where the whole of line 12 gave $11,999 and denied it). Boundary pair: $10,749 + $1,200 = $11,949, allowed; $10,799 + $1,200 = $11,999, denied.

Fact.Name: Below EITC Investment Income Limit
Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer's EIC "investment income" (Form 1040 Step 2) is at or below the $11,950 limit (§32(i); Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §.06). Computes Pub 596 (2025) Worksheet 1 line 14 = interest (L1, 1040 line 2b) + tax-exempt interest (L2, line 2a) + ordinary dividends (L3, line 3b) + L7 (capital-gain net income LESS the Form 4797 §1231 gain — WS-1 lines 5−6, floored) + L10 (net royalty income, floored) + L13 (net passive-activity income, floored). This ADDS Form 1040 Step 2 Q3/Q4, previously unimplemented (the gate was only Q1+Q2 = interest + dividends + gross capital gain). The §1231 subtraction (L7) discharges the EIC-wrongly-DENIED divergence; the royalty + passive terms (L10, L13) discharge the EIC-wrongly-ALLOWED (refundable-credit-paid-in-error) divergence. Identical to the plain sum for a filer with no §1231 gain / royalty / net passive income (L6=0 ⇒ L7=L5; L10=L13=0). L2 (Form 8814 line 1b tax-exempt interest) and L4 (Form 8814 line 12 other income over $2,700) are both directly computed: /eitcInvestmentIncome sums each over every elected child and adds it into this fact, so a Form 8814 election RAISES investment income and can deny the credit on its own merits rather than being refused or silently zeroed. The personal-property-rental and farm-rental terms remain not-modelled 0-stubs — a disclosed intake gap, not a refusal. L13 now ALSO combines a Form 4797 line 10 passive ordinary gain/loss (/form4797Line10PassiveOrdinaryGain, the complete-safe wrapper over /writableForm4797Line10PassiveOrdinaryGain) with /overallPassiveNet BEFORE the floor, per WS-1's own line-13 instruction to combine lines 11 and 12 (the gains and losses) and floor once — not floor each term separately, which would wrongly deny the EIC to a filer whose passive GAIN from one activity is offset by a passive LOSS from another. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Main home was in the U.S. for more than half the year (Form 1040 page 1 checkbox)
Fact.Description:
The Form 1040 page-1 attestation: "Check here if your main home, and your spouse's if filing a joint return, was in the U.S. for more than half of 2025" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040.pdf, page 1). One Boolean for the return, matching the single printed checkbox, which already covers both spouses.
IT IS AN ELIGIBILITY CONDITION FOR THE CHILDLESS EITC, not a decoration. Publication 596 Rule 14 — "You Must Have Lived in the United States More Than Half of the Year ... Your home (and your spouse's if filing a joint return) must have been in the United States for more than half the year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p596.pdf, page 19) — and the publication's own eligibility checklist puts it on the no-qualifying-child path: "If you don't have a qualifying child ... skip questions 8 and 9 and answer 10-12", question 12 being this test citing Rule 14 (lines 1550-1561).
"UNITED STATES" HERE EXCLUDES THE TERRITORIES, and that is printed too: "United States. This means the 50 states and the District of Columbia. It doesn't include Puerto Rico or U.S. territories such as Guam" (lines 1217-1220). That sentence is why Publication 1321 can say flatly that a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico cannot claim the EITC — it is a CONSEQUENCE of this rule and of "employee pay is earned income only if it is taxable", not a separate statutory bar. Neither Publication 596 nor IRC section 32 contains one.
UNANSWERED IS TREATED AS IN THE U.S., which is exactly today's behaviour and is why this change moves no committed return. THE DIRECTION OF THAT TAIL IS TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE and is stated rather than buried: a filer whose main home was NOT in the U.S. and who is never asked keeps a credit Rule 14 denies. The alternative tail — unanswered means NOT in the U.S. — would deny the childless EITC to every return in the corpus, which is both wrong and a far larger error than the one being fixed.

Fact.Name: Main home in the U.S. for more than half of 2025, counting time stationed abroad on extended active duty (IRC 32(c)(4))
Fact.Description:
User response: counting the time the filer, or the filer's spouse if filing jointly, was stationed outside the United States on extended active duty with the U.S. Armed Forces as time in the United States, was the main home in the United States for more than half of 2025?
WHY THE QUESTION COUNTS TIME AND DOES NOT ASK STATUS. IRC 32(c)(4) treats the member's principal place of abode as in the United States "during any period" the member is stationed abroad on extended active duty. It adds that period to the time at home; it does not satisfy the more-than-half-year test by itself. A member stationed abroad for one month who lived abroad as a civilian for the rest of the year has not met the test, and a question asking only whether the filer was ever stationed abroad would pass that filer.
QUESTION TEXT, as it should be asked: "Counting the time you (or your spouse, if filing jointly) were stationed outside the U.S. on extended active duty as time in the U.S., was your main home in the U.S. for more than half of 2025?"
HELP TEXT: "If you or your spouse were stationed outside the United States on extended active duty with the U.S. Armed Forces, the law treats your home as in the United States for the time you were stationed abroad. Add that time to the time your main home was in the United States. Extended active duty means a call or order to duty for more than 90 days or for an indefinite period."
ASKED WHEN: the filer answered No to /writableMainHomeInUsOverHalfYear, or a qualifying child lived with the filer in the United States for less than half the year, and the filer or the spouse was stationed outside the United States on extended active duty at some time in 2025. A filer who already answered the main-home question Yes needs no exception.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: treated as No, the adverse direction: the ordinary answers decide, as they do for a filer never stationed abroad.
VALIDATION: Boolean. Yes/No radio, no default selection.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /mainHomeInUsOverHalfYear (the childless-credit test, IRC 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(I)) and familyAndHousehold:/familyAndHousehold/*/livedWithTpInUsMostOfYear (the qualifying-child test, IRC 32(c)(3)(C)), through the complete-safe /mainHomeInUsOverHalfYearCountingExtendedActiveDutyAbroad.

THE SECTION 32(c)(1)(C) FORM 2555 DISQUALIFICATION. IRC 32(c)(1)(C), "Exception for individual claiming benefits under section 911": "The term 'eligible individual' does not include any individual who claims the benefits of section 911 (relating to citizens or residents living abroad) for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 32, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section32&num=0&edition=2024). The Form 1040 instructions put the same rule as step 3 of the EIC eligibility flowchart: "3. Are you filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income)? ... Yes. STOP You can't take the credit" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 40, a two-column layout in which the word "credit." falls on line 2614).
IT IS A TOTAL DISQUALIFICATION, NOT AN INCOME ADJUSTMENT, which is why it is one more conjunct here rather than a worksheet line: the filer is not an eligible individual at all, no amount enters and no limit moves. That is also why the term reads the FACT of filing and not an exclusion amount — the statute has no dollar threshold anywhere in it, so an amount edge would imply a test Congress did not write.
IT READS THE SHARED GATE, NOT AN EITC-LOCAL BOOLEAN. form2555 /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is the one place a return can assert "I file Form 2555"; six modules converge on it. A single-module EITC writable would have made that assertion representable while seven other modules' MAGI and eligibility computations stayed silently wrong for the same return.
ADDITIVE ON THE WHOLE COMMITTED CORPUS, and the trio below is what proves it rather than asserts it. The gate resolves COMPLETE FALSE when the attestation is unanswered (its IsComplete/Switch guard), which every committed scenario is, so Not(gate) is TRUE and this All() resolves exactly as it would without this conjunct. Complete-false and not Incomplete is the load-bearing half: an Incomplete term inside this All() would take EITC eligibility Incomplete for every return in the dictionary. Examples: unanswered, this fact stays TRUE and the credit stays $2; on an identical return with the attestation YES, this fact goes FALSE and Form 1040 line 27 goes to zero; answered NO, the credit is allowed.
WORLD-1 DIRECTION: taxpayer-UNFAVOURABLE for the population it opens, because it denies a credit. That direction is the statute's, and the alternative is worse — a Form 2555 filer who keeps the EITC because the software never asked. The population is not reachable today in any case: form2555 /knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses any return that answers the attestation yes, and this change is one of the three whose joint completion retires that refusal (with preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetTax and form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback).
THE SECTION 32(e) FULL-YEAR RULE. IRC 32(e) allows no credit for a taxable year of less than 12 months, except a year closed by the taxpayer's death. The only other short year an individual return here can carry is a section 443(a)(1) change of annual accounting period, which standardDeduction /filesShortPeriodReturnForAccountingPeriodChange attests; a return that answers it yes is not eligible. That reading is complete-safe FALSE when the question is unanswered, so every return that does not answer it is unaffected. Answered yes, the credit is denied; answered no, it is kept.

Fact.Name: The filer elected not to claim the earned income credit, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete safe reading of /writableDoesNotWantToClaimEitc, the Form 1040 line 27c election: true when the filer checked the box, and FALSE both when they answered no and when the question was never asked. The intake is a bare Boolean Writable, so a raw Dependency on it inside the /earnedIncomeCredit Switch would blank the credit - and everything downstream of it - on every return that never reached the question. FALSE IS THE ONLY SAFE DEFAULT HERE: it leaves the credit standing, so no filer can lose the EIC by silence, and the only way to reach the $0 arm is to have said so.

Fact.Name: Clergy dual-reported Schedule SE income (EIC Step 5/Worksheet B line 1 subtraction)
Fact.Description:
How much of the amount on Form 1040 line 1z was ALSO reported on Schedule SE, Part I, line 2? A minister, member of a religious order (no vow of poverty), or Christian Science practitioner paid as a W-2 employee for ministerial services is still treated as self-employed for self-employment tax on those SAME earnings (IRC 1402(c)), so the identical dollar amount can sit in BOTH Form 1040 line 1z (wages) and Schedule SE line 2 (net earnings from self-employment). Counting it in EIC earned income twice would overstate the credit's earned-income base; the IRS instructions require backing the overlap OUT of the wage side before it reaches the worksheet.
ASKED WHEN: /writableIsClergyFilingScheduleSE is true (i.e. Form 1040 line 27b is checked) — follow-up to that box, not a screen shown to every filer.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. The filer has already told the IRS (by checking line 27b) that an overlap exists; the amount is a fact only the filer holds (this dictionary has no independent way to compute how much of a minister's W-2 wages Schedule SE line 2 also counts), so an unanswered amount here leaves /eitcClergyDualReportedIncomeSubtrahend, and therefore /eitcEarnedIncomeBase and everything the EITC computes from it, Incomplete rather than silently treating the overlap as $0 (which would leave the double-count in place and contradict the box the filer just checked): no silent favourable default on a claiming return.
VALIDATION: Dollar, non-negative (Min $0). No stated upper bound in the instructions, but the amount cannot exceed either Form 1040 line 1z or Schedule SE line 2 in practice; this dictionary does not cross-check the two (the same posture as the sibling Medicaid-waiver and inmate/workfare subtrahends, whose own Descriptions carry the same disclosed limit) and relies on the final GreaterOf(...,0) floor at /eitcEarnedIncomeBase to keep earned income non-negative on a data-entry error.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /eitcClergyDualReportedIncomeSubtrahend, which /eitcEarnedIncomeBase reads as a sixth subtrahend from the wage-side minuend term.

Fact.Name: EIC earned income: foreign-government wages reported on both Form 1040 line 1h and Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description:
The amount of a U.S. citizen's wages from a foreign government or international organization (IRC 1402(c)(2)(C), no Form W-2) that is on Form 1040 line 1h AND on Schedule SE line 2, for each filer the lesser of the two, rounded to the dollar as both printed lines are. /eitcEarnedIncomeBase subtracts it so the same wages count once in EIC earned income: IRC 32(c)(2)(A) adds employee compensation and net earnings from self-employment, two categories of amounts, and a single amount that falls in both is still one amount of earned income. The subtraction follows the only printed treatment of dual-reported earned income, the EIC Clergy and Church employees instructions, which take the amount out of the Step 5 line 1 wage figure and keep it in the self-employment figure.
THE SPOUSE'S TERM follows the first addend of /eitcEarnedIncomeBase: on a community property allocation return that addend is the primary filer's alone, so only the primary filer's overlap is subtracted there.
Complete-safe: $0 on every return with no such wages. Incomplete only where Schedule SE's own location question is unanswered on a return that entered the wages, which is already a refusal upstream.

Fact.Name: EIC Step 5 line 1 clergy subtraction — the amount also reported on Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description: The clergy dual-reporting subtrahend /eitcEarnedIncomeBase reads: $0 when this return owes no self-employment tax at all (the clergy overlap is structurally impossible — MOOT, checked first so the vast majority of filers who never see the line 27b screen are never asked about it and never blocked by it), $0 when /writableIsClergyFilingScheduleSE reads Complete false (decisively unchecked — the ordinary case for an SE-owing filer who is not clergy), and the attested, whole-dollar amount (/writableClergyDualReportedScheduleSeIncome) when the box reads Complete true AND the amount is answered. NO FOURTH ARM: on an SE-owing return the box is a REQUIRED question, not an optional one defaulted to false when silent — a filer who has checked line 27b has told the IRS an overlap exists, and one who has NOT yet answered it, on a return that DOES owe self-employment tax, is a claiming return with an open condition of allowance. BOTH an unanswered checkbox on an SE-owing return AND a checked-TRUE box with an unanswered dollar amount fall off the end of this Switch and resolve Incomplete — the same no-default idiom form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 already uses.

Fact.Name: Schedule EIC line 6 months the child lived with the taxpayer in the United States, as the printed numeral
Fact.Description:
Schedule EIC LINE 6, printed in full as "Number of months child lived with you in the United States during 2025". The graph stores the answer as a bucket Enum over /monthsLivedWithTPInUSOptions (twelve, eleven, ten, nine, eight, seven, six); the printed box wants a numeral, so this fact maps each option to the string the form prints. SIX MAPS TO 7, NOT 6, and that is the printed rule rather than a rounding: "If the child lived with you for more than half of 2025 but less than 7 months, enter 7." The six bucket IS that case, because a child who lived with the taxpayer for six months or fewer and still qualifies did so for more than half the year. The seven case also prints 7. PORTED, NOT INVENTED: these are the seven cases upstream IRS Direct File filled in the filler as customMaps.transformMonthsLived, recorded in the FIELD-DRIFT header of dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040EIC/en/configuration.yml. Building it in the dictionary rather than as a `~` transform keeps the printed numeral in the fact graph where it can be tested.
THE PRINTED LINE'S SECOND OVERRIDE, enter 12 for a child born or died in 2025 whose home was the taxpayer's home for more than half the time they were alive during 2025, is honoured FIRST, ahead of the month-bucket mapping: familyAndHousehold:../bornOrDiedResidencyException is that exact test (born or died in the tax year AND the taxpayer's home was the child's home for more than half the time they were alive), and it can be true when the bucket Enum was never answered at all, because a child born late in the year cannot truthfully choose any of the six-through-twelve options the bucket offers. The default arm prints the empty string on an unanswered bucket. THE PRINTED LINE'S THIRD OVERRIDE, and it is honoured AHEAD of both: a kidnapped qualifying child meeting the IRC 152(f)(6) requirements enters "KC" instead of a number. familyAndHousehold:../kidnappedChildResidencyException is that test, and it is read here through All(IsComplete(x), x) because it is deliberately not complete-safe - on a return that claims the exception and leaves a condition of allowance blank it resolves Incomplete, and such a return is stopped by flow:/flowIncomplete before anything prints.
PRINT ONLY: nothing computes from this fact, and the EIC itself reads the residency test, not this numeral. THE MeF ELEMENT for a "KC" line 6 entry is not in this repo's sources, so nothing is claimed about the electronic shape; this fact is Export downstreamFacts, not mef, and the paper binding in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040EIC/en/configuration.yml already carries it unchanged. interpretation:provisional.
